samples.summary: A boundary-refused subtree also swallows its explicitly selected descendants, so "select the whole list → Shift+Tab" (or Tab) is now a total no-op where it previously moved the nested items
samples.evidence: planSiblingGroup adds every subtree member to `covered` (line 90) *before* the floor/ceiling checks at lines 93-94, then `continue`s on refusal. So for blocks [a(0), b(1)] with BOTH selected and delta=-1: a is refused (level 0), b is already in `covered`, and the loop skips it → zero changes. The old code (text-editor.ts handleTab, editor.ts outdent) computed `Math.max(0, cur-1)` per selected block, so b went 1→0 and only a was skipped — which is also what Google Docs does. Same for indent: [a(7), b(8)] both selected used to raise a to 8; now the whole selection is refused because `deepest >= MAX_LIST_LEVEL`. The result is a common gesture (select an entire nested list, press Shift+Tab) silently doing nothing. The tests in test/model/list-level.test.ts bless this as intended, so it may be a deliberate design call — but it is a behavior regression on a normal path and worth confirming.

samples.summary: `siblingsOf` resolves the caret's container from the layout-time parent map; when that map has no entry for a cell block (created since the last layout) the returned sibling array does not contain the block, and the whole indent/outdent gesture becomes a silent no-op
samples.evidence: `siblingsOf` returns `doc.getContextBlocks()` when `doc.blockParentMap.get(block.id)` is undefined (editor.ts:1640; the same shape in text-editor.ts:2892 via `getActiveLayout().blockParentMap`). The map is only rebuilt in `recomputeLayout`, and `Doc.findBlockInCells` documents exactly this staleness ("a block created since the last layout — e.g. the tail block a paste splits out inside a cell — isn't in it yet", document.ts:259-262) which is why it keeps a full-walk fallback. `siblingsOf` has no such fallback. For a cell-internal caret missing from the map, siblings resolve to the region's top-level blocks; `planSiblingGroup` then never finds the selected id in `blocks` and emits zero changes, so indent/outdent does nothing at all. Before this change `fn(block)` applied the level unconditionally, so the gesture always worked.

samples.summary: `TextEditor.siblingsOf` uses the throwing `getBlock` for the parent-table lookup where the editor.ts twin deliberately uses non-throwing `findBlock`
samples.evidence: text-editor.ts:2893 `const tableBlock = this.doc.getBlock(info.tableBlockId);` — `Doc.getBlock` throws `Block not found` (document.ts:215). editor.ts:1641 uses `doc.findBlock` precisely to avoid that ("a table removed since then would throw out of the middle of an indent gesture rather than degrade to the block alone"). Since the parent map is only as fresh as the last layout pass, a stale `tableBlockId` throws out of handleIndent/handleOutdent/handleTab here. Reach is limited because `this.doc.getBlock(this.cursor.position.blockId)` on line 2878 would usually throw first for the same staleness, hence minor.

samples.summary: The new `levelOf` normalization only guards the planner; the layout and paint reads of `listLevel` still consume the raw peer value, so a NaN/Infinite level from a remote Tree attribute still produces NaN geometry until a gesture happens to touch that block
samples.evidence: list-level.ts:29-33 normalizes on read and its doc comment explicitly notes the layout pass "reads `listLevel` raw", but nothing in this change fixes that read: layout.ts:494 `LIST_INDENT_PX * ((block.listLevel ?? 0) + 1)`, table-layout.ts:93 and paint-layout.ts:198 all use the value verbatim. A poisoned level therefore still yields NaN marginLeft / marker x for every block that is never indented or outdented. The planner's repair-on-write only heals blocks a user gesture moves.

samples.summary: Indenting a selected child whose parent is not selected still widens the parent/child gap to two levels; the planner normalizes poisoned values but never re-normalizes the resulting hierarchy
samples.evidence: For [a(0), b(1)] with only b selected and delta=+1, planSiblingGroup emits b→2 (line 102). Adjacency-implied nesting now has a two-level jump under a level-0 parent, the same class of malformed tree the module exists to prevent. This matches the pre-change behavior, so it is not a regression — noting it because the module's stated invariant ("a parent stays a parent") does not cover it.

verdict.reason: The quoted code exists exactly as described: planSiblingGroup adds the whole subtree to `covered` at list-level.ts:90 before the floor/ceiling checks at :93-94, so [a(0), b(1)] both selected with delta=-1 yields zero changes. However, this is not a logic defect — it is the explicitly specified behavior of the change, recorded in three places in this repo: the task decision list (todo.md:30-38, decisions #3 and #4: "A subtree whose root was refused by a boundary also suppresses its selected descendants"), the design doc (docs.md:160-169: "relative depth is preserved, or nothing moves … skipped, refused or not, so … a refused parent never leaves its selected child to flatten on its own"), and the unit tests that state the rationale inline (list-level.test.ts:79-85, 92-97). The implementation matches that intent exactly and uniformly at all six writers. There is no crash, no data loss, no partial application (the plan is computed whole, then applied), and no inconsistent state — the gesture is a recoverable no-op. What is left is a disagreement with a deliberate, documented product/UX trade-off (refuse-as-a-unit vs. per-block clamping, the latter being the #1050 symptom), which the correctness lens defers to design/product. I also confirmed `covered` cannot absorb non-descendants: subtreeOf (:46-62) only extends over contiguous list-items at strictly greater level and levelOf (:29-33) normalizes NaN/Infinity, so the suppression is bounded to the genuine subtree.
